_about: WHAT THE RUN ASKS OF THE ENGINE'S OPTIONAL PERFORMANCE FEATURES, and of the port's own per-frame diagnostics.
Planning step 190 of docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md (ENG-3). Read by sim/EngineTuning; main.cpp turns it into the
engine's GameManifest fields (engine/src/core/GameRuntime.hpp) and the layer's Paths::spriteReport. A table that will not read leaves the
engine AS IT WAS, with a WARN in the log. The log's third line says what the run was given: 'engine options (a player's run): ...'.
A player's run (attended_run) is a window the game opened for someone to play (game/RunKind.hpp, AttendedRun); every capture, route, level
walk and script is 'other_runs'. The flags --shadow-maps, --sprites-only, --asset-watching, --sprite-report and --perf-log override this
table for ONE run (an A/B: one exe, one setting changed). To decline a value, change it here: no code changes, no relink.
Each value is a MEASURED decision. The rule it had to meet: every picture byte for byte what it was (the 19 classic baselines in 9 variants, 162 launches,
the 128-level f420 sweep under three configurations, the S/R/W pictures) AND a measured gain on a named metric. All measurements: Magic Portals Enhanced, AMD
Radeon 780M (integrated), Windows 11, 1280x720, present mode FIFO (60 fps), Vulkan validation layers ON, MagicPortals.exe a0a9f233, 2026-10-16;
medians of 3 interleaved launches (the numbers are for A/B, not a player's frame rate).
shadow_map_resolution 16 (KEPT): no sprite samples a shadow map. The developer's lit boxes do: with the B key pressed over level12b's art,
165,280 of 921,600 pixels (17.9%) differ between 16 px and the engine's own sizes (the boxes' shadows are gone; a real-time run, a synthetic
B keypress); a level run with an empty --art folder gives 166,165 (18.0%) and level0 8; --shadow-maps 0 brings them back. The art view,
which is what a player sees, is byte for byte the same. The GPU memory of the process (Windows' per-process counter, level12b at
5 s) fell from 350.6 to 157.8 MiB dedicated (-192.8; total committed 410.9 to 218.2), on both launches of each; pictures identical.
The engine's own sizes are 4 x 2048 + 2 x 1024 + 2 x 1024 D32 (120 MiB by arithmetic; the counter also holds the driver's alignment).
sprites_only_scene_pipelines false (DECLINED; the mechanism stays, --sprites-only on): every draw this port puts through the scene pipelines is
unlit (a sprite, a particle, a halo), so the four pipelines can be built with the lit surface folded away, and with it on every picture was byte
for byte what it was (the 19 baselines, the 128-level sweep, the S/R/W pictures). Declined because no gain could be measured here and a small
cost was: the four scene pipelines take 37 ms (35..48) to create at every warm start against 31 ms (29..36) plain, 13 launches each (retaken on
the final exe, 6 launches each: 37.5 ms (36..44) against 35.5 (33..40), so the cost is 2 to 6 ms at every warm start); the first
compile ever is cheaper (315 ms against 641 ms, two single cold launches on different days, not a controlled pair); and no GPU time can be
measured on a 60 fps FIFO machine. The gain the engine's author measured is on an Adreno 640 (a 2D menu in 75 ms instead of 117): when a phone
build exists, set this true and take the pictures gate there. The cost of true: the developer's lit boxes (the B key, and a level drawn without
its art) draw flat; --sprites-only off brings them back.
asset_watching attended_run false (KEPT): the engine stats every watched file on every frame for a developer's hot reload and hashes every
material's paths. Process CPU time over a 600-frame run (GetProcessTimes), on versus off: still level 2562 (2219..2891) to 2016 (1922..2062)
ms, route 2703 to 2359 ms, scrolling 1875 to 1594 ms (420 frames): 0.57 to 0.91 ms of CPU per frame, the ranges not overlapping (retaken on
the final exe: still 0.57, scrolling 0.78, route 0.68). Pictures identical. The wall time of 600 frames is the same on and off (about 10.9 s:
a FIFO loop is paced by the display). other_runs stays true so parity work keeps hot reload.
sprite_report attended_run true (DECLINED): the layer's per-frame walk over its sprites for the 'on'/'off'/'GONE' log lines. Game Layers
median 0.1514 ms on, 0.1479 off (ranges overlap, the noise floor is about 0.004 ms), no change on the scrolling or route runs; in a real
console window the first second's worst frame is 214 to 219 ms either way. Not kept: nothing measurable. The switch stays (--sprite-report).
mobile (planning step 201, PORT-3): the PHONE PROFILE, laid over the answers above for a run under it. A phone's build runs under it by default
(game/BuildProfile.hpp kMobileBuild); `--profile mobile` asks the same of a desktop run, `--profile desktop` the other way. A desktop run never
reads the block, but this file is checked whole when it is loaded, so a typo in it fails where the file is read. Its keys are described in the
block itself. Nothing in it has been measured on a phone: no phone has run this port.
THE PHONE PROFILE: each key here, when present, REPLACES the answer above for a run under the profile (sim/EngineTuning.hpp MobileBlock). A key
left out leaves the desktop's answer. The keys, and only these (any other key that does not begin with an underscore is refused by name):
minimum_vulkan_minor 1 (or 2): the lowest Vulkan 1.x a GPU must report to be used; GameManifest::minimumVulkanMinor (engine/src/core/GameRuntime.hpp:89,
clamped into 1 to 2 by GameRuntime.cpp:117). Without it the engine wants 1.2, and the stock drivers of many phones on Android 11 and 12 report 1.1: no GPU is
acceptable, the device constructor throws and the start ends before its first frame. Source: the sibling port Penumbra and the Castle of Shadows Enhanced, its
step E39, where two testers' phones (an Oppo A54 on Android 11, Vulkan 1.1.131, and an A74 5G on Android 12, 1.1.128) opened to a black screen and the home
screen, and the engine's author states that it uses nothing newer than 1.1 core (GameRuntime.hpp). Decoded from that record and the engine's code; NOT measured
here, on any phone. Unverified on a 1.1 driver: the scene fragment stage uses 8 of one known GPU's 8 combined fragment resources (Penumbra E39).
This is a START/NO-START matter and not a tuning one, which is why it is a key at all and the desktop leaves it out: a desktop run asks for 1.2, the engine's own.
shadow_map_resolution 16: as the top-level key, repeated on purpose. The top-level 16 is a desktop decision (step 190: no sprite samples a shadow map, 192.8 MiB
of GPU memory saved on a 780M); on a phone the system's low-memory manager counts those bytes, and the sibling port's E43 took the same 16 for it. Written here
so that a developer who sets the top-level key to 0 to see the lit boxes' shadows does not move a phone with it.
asset_watching false: the engine's per-frame stat of every watched file (step 190: 0.57 to 0.91 ms of CPU a frame on the desktop). On a phone the texture keys are
virtual and not files at all, so every stat fails every frame (engine/src/core/GameRuntime.hpp, assetWatching). A plain true/false, for both kinds of run: a
phone has nobody to hot-reload a saved file for. A desktop run's attended answer is already false, so for a player the key says it again.
KEYS THAT DO NOT EXIST YET, on purpose (the _decision_pending note below names them): nothing here turns the scene's sample cap or dynamic resolution on, and no
reader exists for a key that would.

_decision_pending.scene_samples: OWNER DECISION, with edge_cover.enabled and dynamic resolution as one bundle (the platform research's PL-05, owner decision 1): 1 or 2 samples would save 44 or 24 B per pixel of the scene target but move a few percent of edge pixels in a project whose gate is pixels. Could change a pixel. No key, no reader.
_decision_pending.dynamic_resolution: OWNER DECISION and the phone-profile step: the scene target sized by how fast the GPU draws it, and the HUD and controls blur with it. Inert for --fixed-step and --screenshot, so it could not change a captured pixel, but it changes what a player sees. No key, no reader.
_decision_pending.sprites_only_scene_pipelines: The phone-profile step: byte-identical in every picture of this port on a desktop (step 190) and a measured gain only on an Adreno 640 in the sibling port; true for a phone is proposed, not decided. Could change a pixel only of the developer's lit boxes. No mobile key; the top-level key (false) applies.
_decision_pending.sprite_report: The phone-profile step: the layer's per-frame log walk; false for a phone is proposed. Changes no pixel. No mobile key; the top-level key applies.
